description.en:
San Antonio de Padua, patron of lost things, was one of the many statuettes Rizal made during his exile in Dapitan. The heads of both the saint and the Infant Jesus were lost, the piece was restored with abaca.

It is kept in the Museo ni Jose Rizal in Fort Santiago and displayed during Rizal-related events.
description.fil:
Si San Antonio de Padua, patron ng mga bagay na nawawala, ay isa sa maraming estatwilyang ginawa ni Rizal noong panahon ng kanyang pagkakatapon sa Dapitan. Nawala ang mga ulo ng santo at ng Sanggol na Hesus, at isinaayos ang piyesa gamit ang abaka.

Nakatago ito sa Museo ni Jose Rizal sa Fort Santiago at itinatanghal sa mga okasyong may kaugnayan kay Rizal.
description.de:
San Antonio de Padua, der Schutzpatron der verlorenen Dinge, war eine der vielen Statuetten, die Rizal während seiner Verbannung in Dapitan schuf. Die Köpfe des Heiligen und des Christuskinds gingen verloren, das Stück wurde mit Abaka ergänzt.

Es wird im Museo ni Jose Rizal in Fort Santiago bewahrt und bei Veranstaltungen rund um Rizal gezeigt.

images.alt: Weathered statuette of Saint Anthony of Padua holding the Infant Jesus, both figures missing their heads, on a square plinth
Close view of the saint's hooded habit, broken off at the neck where the head was lost
Detail of the saint's hands cradling the headless Infant Jesus
The saint's knees and feet, with the twisted abaca cord running down the front of the habit
Close view of the stepped base, the frayed end of the abaca cord and the incised marks on the plinth
Postcard from 1911 reproducing a photograph of the statuette when it was still intact, with both heads in place and “Rizal” carved on the base
